Session Score

Listener guide

Hear your local Codex sessions as music. A bass melody runs during work, and reads, edits and commands add parts to the track. These screenshots use a sample session.

Install Node.js 22 or later. In the project folder, run npm run dev and open the address printed in the terminal.

Listen to a sessionShape the musicEarlier terminal player

No matching features.

Listen to a session

Choose a starting sound

Pick Classical, Electronic or Hyperpop. Each preset remembers its own settings.

Link all Codex sessions

Turn on Link all Codex. The link stays ready while sessions are idle. The next working session starts the bass.

Follow a read, edit and command

The Activity list identifies each action and its source session. In this guide capture, a seeded file read adds keys, an edit adds chords and a command adds a groove.

Shape the music

Hold a bass melody and mix the layers

Choose Undertow and Hold selected melody to keep one line underneath the action. A playing session picks up the change at the next four-bar boundary. Use the channel sliders to balance the parts.

Explore the variation inventory

Compare the ten bass lines and see what each action can play. Steady uses one version, Subtle uses two and Evolving uses three.

Give each action a musical role

Choose a part and instrument for each action. Length controls how many bars it plays while work continues. Set Read a file to Evolving to hear related phrases on repeated reads.

Save or share your settings

Edits save in this browser. Export settings downloads the selected preset as JSON. Import settings restores it, including action rules, bass selection and mixer levels.

Hear the end of a turn

When the last session finishes normally, sounding notes fade for up to 0.8 seconds. The link stays ready for the next turn. Disconnect audio switches it off.

Earlier terminal player

Use the earlier Turbella player

The optional Python player follows one Turbella session. Install the dependencies from requirements.txt, find the session ID in the local Turbella status output, then pass it to play_live.py with the groove or electronic preset.

Terminal transcript
$ python3 play_live.py --help
usage: play_live.py [-h] [--preset {groove,electronic}] session

Play new Turbella events for one Codex session as a live groove.

positional arguments:
  session

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --preset {groove,electronic}

Exit 0
